title: Player record — one shape, every sport
status: PROPOSED - reconciled with the Owner's direction of 2026-10-21. The Owner gives final approval to each pool; the council assembles and reviews.
why_this_shape: The football build's PLAYERS tuple (name, pos, team, ovr, spd, str, agi, cod, inj, awr) is the schema the existing maths already consumes — the value maths reads ovr only (v20:946 effOvr), so a record that keeps ovr intact is a drop-in for the current engine.

One shape across sports is what lets ONE validator, ONE rubric and ONE calibration set serve the NFL, the NBA and the soccer leagues. Sport-specific facts (NBA shooting splits, soccer positions) live in an OPTIONAL extension block, never in a second schema.

The five layers mirror GPT's DATA_AND_RATING_STANDARD: source observation -> normalized record -> rating transformation -> mode adjustment -> simulation input. Collapsing them is how 'where did this number come from' becomes unanswerable.

record.id: stable person id, lowercase ascii, unique in the pool, NEVER derived from the display name (the intake contains 3 same-name different-person collisions and 69 shared surnames)
record.name: display name, disambiguated where needed ('Steve Smith (1958-2016)')
aliases: other spellings of the same person
position_candidates: position codes the sources support, with the conflict flagged when they disagree (the intake has 70 such names)
record.modern_franchise: the CURRENT franchise used by the simulation (Owner direction: today's franchises, always)
record.historical_franchise: the historical team, for DRAFT-BOARD CONTEXT ONLY (Owner direction: e.g. Oscar Robertson's Cincinnati Royals, while the simulation places him on the current Sacramento Kings). Never used by the engine.

career_status.source: where the status comes from; a roster career span is not a retirement source

record.ovr: INTEGER 40..99 - the simulation rating and the general player summary (Owner: public-facing data is integers; internal maths may use decimals, but do not publish decimals)

attributes.note: a small number of attributes the engine actually uses, integers, each with a stated consumer. Do not add fields the engine does not use. In the football build only ovr reaches the value maths; spd/agi/cod/awr are used by one function (returnerRating) and inj by none.

record.extensions: OPTIONAL, integer-only, sport-specific display context (NBA: TS+, three-point rate; football: none today). Not consumed by the engine unless a consumer is named.

source.id: the source record id (e.g. NFL-AT-001, an NBA2K export with edition/year/season)
source.class: owner-supplied notes | official roster | 2K export | council rating
source.note: what the source actually says - a mention, a roster line, a rating. A mention is not a rating.

meta.candidate_target: 1500-2000 candidates per sport (Owner direction, 2026-10-21). A pool only needs enough players to fill the required positions and rosters; a draft does not have to use every eligible player.
meta.current_player_adjustment: NOT APPROVED as of 2026-10-21. Do not apply a -5 (or any) adjustment until its purpose, eligible players and calibration are decided. Until then, current players carry their current rating.
meta.approval: the Owner approves the final pool; the council assembles and reviews

rules: A record's OVR is what the engine consumes; the six attributes are consumed today only by the special-teams returner rating (v20:2581). Rating work should therefore put the care into OVR and the provenance.
A record may not be published without provenance.source, source_date, rater(s) and rubric version.
A mode adjustment is a separate, versioned field — never a permanent edit of the source rating.
Historical position codes are translated to current slot families by the taxonomy at LOAD time, so the flex table and the weights never see a legacy code.
The pool stores a pool_rank; the published target is a filter on it. Changing the target is a filter change, not a re-rating.

LEGAL VOCABULARY: a position code is legal if it appears in the build's NATURAL_SLOT_MAP (the 19 draftable codes) OR in the build's own player vocabulary (FB, P, LS — present in the pool, never drafted). A code that is neither is a legacy/unknown code: those records are invisible to the draft pool, the replacement levels and the slot maps, and the draft then silently skips the picks it cannot fill (M-81).

The published reference pool is data/nfl/current.json — 1,200 records exported verbatim from the reference build by tools/export-current-pool.mjs and validated by tools/validate-dataset.mjs (exit 0). It is the file to copy the shape from.

SAME NAMES ARE NEVER MERGED: the all-time intake scan found 3 same-name/different-person collisions (Larry Johnson, Steve Smith, Joe Johnson) and 69 shared surnames among 1,470 distinct names. A pool record therefore carries a stable `id` (never derived from the display name) and a DISAMBIGUATED display name (e.g. 'Steve Smith (1958-2016)'), with `aliases` holding the other spellings. Never merge two records because their names match, and never let a name-only join create a record.

THE -5 CURRENT-PLAYER ADJUSTMENT IS NOT APPROVED (Owner, 2026-10-21). It must not appear in any pool until its purpose, eligible players and calibration are decided. The mode-adjustment FIELD remains in the schema so a future approved adjustment has a home, but it stays empty.
PUBLIC DATA IS INTEGERS. Internal calculations may use decimals; do not publish decimal ratings and do not invent fields the engine does not use.

MODERN RULES. Simulation rules are the current rules of the sport; for all-time players the Owner's modeling assumption is a year of training under modern rules - an assumption to argue from evidence, never a formula.
TODAY'S FRANCHISES. The simulation uses current franchises; the historical team is display context on the draft board only.
KEEP THE SIX THINGS SEPARATE: person, player-season, team/franchise, career status, source, simulation rating. A record that merges them cannot be corrected without re-rating.
SOURCE MATERIAL IS NOT A POOL. A mention, a fan list or a ranking is source material; it becomes a candidate only with provenance, and it becomes a rating only with the Owner's approval.
revision: rev 4 - 2026-10-21: reconciled with the Owner's product direction (PR #4, OWNER-PRODUCT-DIRECTION.md): person / player-season / team / career-status / source / simulation-rating kept DISTINCT, today's franchises for the simulation with historical team as display context, integer public ratings, no unused fields, and the -5 current-player adjustment is NOT approved.

entities.person: the stable identity (id, name, aliases) - who it is
entities.player_season: a person in a specific season (the intake holds 27 same-name multi-season entries in single ranking files)
entities.team_or_franchise: two distinct things: the historical team (display context) and the modern franchise (simulation identity)
entities.career_status: active / retired / unknown, with its own source and confidence - NOT inferred from a roster span
entities.source: what the source said, with its id, class, date and whether it contained a rating
entities.simulation_rating: the OVR the engine consumes, integer, approved by the Owner
